_about: Context-aware scenarios: text variants with "when" only appear when they fit (after a defeat, abroad, married, in debt...), so the same situation reads differently depending on his life.

scenarios.title: 100,000 Followers and a Blue Tick
text: The notification arrives during a team meeting: 100K. A blue tick appears next to his name. {T} notices and announces it to the whole room.

text.t: 100 ribu followers. Verified. In the family WhatsApp group, {MUM} posts the screenshot eleven times.
A hundred thousand people follow a teenager who still can't cook rice. The blue tick arrives on a Tuesday. {SIB} demands a cut.

scenarios.prompt: How do you use the bigger platform?

choices.label: Hire someone to manage it
choices.text: A social media manager starts on Monday. The posts get prettier. The comments say he 'changed'.

choices.label: Keep it personal
choices.text: He keeps posting himself: blurry photos, bad jokes, real moments. Fans love that it's really him.

choices.label: Use it for a cause
choices.text: His first post as a verified account is about the youth pitch in his old neighbourhood. Donations follow.

scenarios.title: One Million
text: One million people follow {J}. His phone has become a different object: brands, fans, strangers, trolls, all at once.

text.t: {Pf} throws a surprise 'one million' party with a cake shaped like a phone. She films everything. Her followers jump too.
One million followers. {Pf} asks, quietly, whether they can keep their home a phone-free zone.

choices.label: Set boundaries: no family, no home
choices.hint: Your partner and family will thank you.
choices.text: He decides: no family, no home, no partner on his accounts. The fans grumble. The people he loves exhale.

choices.label: Monetise it
choices.text: His agent's phone rings off the hook. Paid posts, collaborations, a clothing capsule. The money is serious. So are the comments about 'ads'.

choices.label: Carry on as before
choices.text: He posts a photo of his muddy boots with the caption 'thanks'. That's it. It becomes his most-liked post ever.

scenarios.title: Sponsor Clash at {club}
text: The club's new main sponsor is a direct rival of one of {J}'s personal sponsors. The commercial director wants him in the launch photo, holding their product.

text.t: The board, already cool on {J}, have chosen this moment to sign a sponsor that competes with his own deal. The commercial director's email is three lines long and ends with 'we expect full cooperation'.

choices.label: Do the club shoot
choices.hint: Your own sponsor will be unhappy.
choices.text: He does the photo, smiling, holding the wrong brand. His own sponsor's lawyer sends a letter by Friday.

choices.label: Refuse, citing your contract
choices.text: He refuses politely, contract in hand. The board backs down and remembers.

choices.label: Let your agent find a compromise

ok.text: A shoot where he holds nothing at all and wears a club tracksuit. Everyone is satisfied, nobody is happy. Perfect.

bad.text: The compromise fails. Both sides are now slightly annoyed.

scenarios.title: {BRAND} Shoot the Day Before a Match
text: {BRAND} have booked a six-hour shoot the day before a match. The location is two hours away. The fitness coach has gone pale.

text.t: {BRAND} want a full-day shoot on Friday. Since {J} isn't starting anyway, the agent says, 'what's the harm?' The harm is that the manager might hear.

choices.label: Go, but cut it to two hours
choices.text: Two hours, efficient, done. The photographer complains. The fitness coach doesn't.

choices.label: Do the full day
choices.text: Six hours under hot lights. On matchday his legs feel like someone else's.

choices.label: Postpone it
choices.text: {BRAND} reschedule, coldly. Their next email is shorter than usual.

scenarios.title: A Bigger Brand Slides Into the DMs
scenarios.text: {BRAND} contact {J} directly on social media, bypassing his agent: 'We'd love to talk about something bigger.' The offer they hint at is double what he earns from his current deal.

choices.label: Forward it to your agent
choices.text: His agent takes it from there. Whatever happens, it happens the right way.

out.text: The conversation goes well — until the agent finds out from the brand's own lawyer. He is furious.
It leads nowhere. Just a strange late-night chat with a marketing executive.

scenarios.title: Tax Season
text: The tax forms are forty pages long. {J} understands about four of them.

text.t: Playing abroad means two tax systems, two sets of rules, and a lot of paperwork in a language he can barely read.
Sponsorship income, image rights, appearance fees: his tax situation has become a full-time job for somebody. That somebody is currently nobody.

choices.label: Hire a proper tax adviser
choices.text: The adviser finds savings he didn't know existed and two mistakes he didn't know he'd made.

out.text: The guy saves him a fortune. Nobody asks how. Yet.
The tax office opens an investigation into the guy's clients. {J}'s name is on the list.

choices.label: Do it yourself
choices.text: Three nights, two headaches, one form submitted late. A fine arrives a month later.

scenarios.title: The Tax Office Calls
scenarios.text: The tax office has opened an audit into the 'creative' accountant {J}'s teammate recommended years ago. Every client is being checked. {J} is a client.

choices.label: Pay everything back, plus penalties
choices.text: He pays. It hurts. The story never reaches the papers.

choices.label: Fight it in court
choices.text: The case drags on for a year and makes every sports page in the country. He wins on a technicality. Nobody remembers the technicality.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Question
text: A former player, now broke at 40, comes to talk to the squad. He made millions. He has nothing. The room is very quiet.

text.t: {J}'s financial adviser lays out two futures on one sheet of paper: the one where he saves now, and the one where he doesn't. The second one ends badly.

choices.label: Set up a pension and investments
choices.desc: Lock away a third of everything.
choices.hint: Less to spend now. Safe later.
choices.text: A third of every payslip goes somewhere he can't touch. Some months it stings. Future {J} will be grateful.

choices.label: Buy property back home
choices.hint: Solid, slow, family helps manage it.
choices.text: He buys two small houses near his parents. {DAD} becomes a landlord and loves it far too much.

choices.label: Later
choices.text: 'Later,' he says. Everyone in the room said that once.

scenarios.title: The Post-Match Microphone

text.t: {J} was the best player on the pitch and the TV crew grab him before he reaches the tunnel, still breathing hard. The reporter is beaming.
After the defeat, the club sends {J} to the mixed zone. Nobody else wanted to go. The reporters are hungry.
A draw nobody can quite explain. {JR} from {OUT} wants three minutes with {J} in the mixed zone.

text: The press officer pushes {J} towards the microphones. 'Two questions, max.' There are going to be more than two questions.

choices.label: Credit the team
choices.text: Humble, generous, a bit boring. The squad reads it on the bus and nods.

choices.label: Speak from the heart
choices.hint: Fans love honesty. Coaches less so.

out.text: His honesty lands. The clip spreads with the caption 'this is why we love him'.
He says one honest thing too many about the tactics. {Mf} reads it the next morning.

choices.label: Make a joke
choices.hint: Charm, if the result allows it.

text.t: The joke lands badly after a defeat. 'He's laughing while we suffer', writes a fan. It trends for a day.
The reporters laugh. The clip is everywhere by dinner, and it's the good kind of everywhere.

scenarios.title: {Pf} Reads the Transfer Rumours
text: {Pf} sends a screenshot of a transfer rumour: a club in another country, a city she's never heard of. Just the screenshot. No words.

text.t: {Pf}'s followers are asking her where she's moving. She doesn't know. She's furious that she has to find out from strangers.
{KID} comes home from school crying: a classmate said they're moving to another country. {Pf} looks at {J} and waits.

scenarios.prompt: Your family is reading about your future in the papers.

choices.label: Sit down and decide together
choices.text: They make a list of places they'd move for and places they wouldn't. It's the most honest conversation they've had in months.

choices.label: 'It's just noise'
choices.text: 'It's nothing.' It isn't nothing to her.

scenarios.title: A Bonus, and a Hole
text: A win bonus lands in {J}'s account. For one day, the balance is almost not negative.

text.t: The bonus arrives, and so does a message from the car dealership: the payment on the car he can't afford is due.

scenarios.prompt: What do you do with the bonus?

choices.label: Every cent goes to the debt
choices.text: It all goes to the bank. The interest bill shrinks. It feels like nothing. It's everything.

choices.label: Treat yourself, you've earned it
choices.text: Dinner, new trainers, a weekend away. The debt is still there on Monday, slightly bigger.

scenarios.title: {BFf} Goes Viral — Because of You
text: A video of {BFf} roasting {J} at a family party goes viral. Now {BFf} has 50,000 followers and brands are messaging him. He's having the time of his life.

text.t: {BFf}, who barely talks to {J} anymore, has become a minor celebrity by posting old stories about him. Some of them are private.

scenarios.prompt: Your best friend is using your fame.

choices.label: Be happy for him
choices.text: You share his best video yourself. His follower count doubles. He sends you a voice note that's mostly screaming.

choices.label: Ask him to keep private things private
choices.text: {BFf} apologises, then deletes two videos. Things are a bit stiff for a while.

scenarios.title: The Run-In
text: The season is in its final stretch. Every training session feels heavier, every mistake louder. The dressing room is quieter than usual.

text.t: {J} is one of the names {Mf} trusts for the run-in. The pressure has a texture now: dry mouth, early mornings, the table on everyone's phone.
The run-in is here and {J} is watching it from the outside. Every day in training is an audition nobody is watching.

scenarios.prompt: How do you handle the final weeks?

choices.label: Lead the young players
choices.text: He takes the nervous academy kids for coffee and tells them about his worst game. They laugh. The tension breaks a little.

choices.label: Lock in completely
choices.desc: No phone, no media, just football.
choices.hint: Focus. Others may feel shut out.
choices.text: He switches everything off: phone, social media, family chat. Pure football.

ok.text: {Mf} likes the hunger. 'Saturday. Don't waste it.'

bad.text: 'Not now,' says {Mf}, and means 'not ever, if you ask like this again'.

scenarios.title: Rehab in Public
text: Injured and bored, {J} gets a message from his agent: rehab content does numbers. Fans want to see the comeback.

text.t: The injury is eating at him, and the comment section isn't helping: 'injury-prone', 'finished', 'waste of money'.

choices.label: Document every step
choices.text: Daily clips: first steps, first jog, first ball. Fans follow every day. When he finally plays again, the whole internet feels it.

choices.label: Go dark until you're back
choices.text: He disappears from social media for weeks. When he comes back, it's with a photo of his boots and one word: 'Back.'

scenarios.title: {KID}'s Birthday Is on Matchday
text: {KID} turns {KIDage} on Saturday. Saturday is matchday. {KID} has asked, seriously, whether the match can be moved.

text.t: {KID}'s birthday party is back home, eight hours' flight away. The match is here, on the same day.

choices.label: Dedicate a goal, video-call the party
choices.text: He tells {KID} on video that if he scores, it's for them. Whatever happens, {KID} watches the whole match in a paper crown.

ok.text: {Mf}, a father himself, says yes. {J} spends the day in a bouncy castle. Best day of the year.

bad.text: {Mf} says no. {J} plays with his mind somewhere else entirely.

scenarios.title: {SIB} Wants to Work for You
text: {SIB} has finished studying and has an idea: become {J}'s manager. Not the football agent — the business manager. Sponsors, money, schedules. 'Who would you trust more than family?'

text.t: {SIB}'s own football career has stalled. {SIBhe} wants to stop playing and start managing {J}'s business instead. 'I know the game. I know you.'

choices.label: Yes, on a proper contract
choices.hint: Could be brilliant. Could ruin Christmas.

out.text: {SIB} turns out to be ferociously good at it. Brands are slightly scared of {SIBhim}. Your mother is the proudest woman alive.
Six months in, they argue about money at a family dinner. {SIB} quits by text. {MUM} cries.

choices.label: Help {SIBhim} find another job
choices.text: You call in a favour with a sponsor. {SIB} gets a marketing job there and, eventually, admits it was the right call.

scenarios.title: {DAD} Could Stop Working
text: {DAD} is {DADage} and still working six days a week. He'll never ask. {MUM} finally does, on his behalf: could {J} help him retire?

text.t: {MUM} calls after weeks of silence. {DAD} has hurt his back at work again. She isn't asking for money. She's asking for her son.

choices.label: Pay him a monthly pension
choices.text: {DAD} argues for an hour, then accepts. On his first Monday off in thirty years he goes fishing and catches nothing and is perfectly happy.

choices.label: Buy him the shop he always wanted
choices.desc: A small business of his own.
choices.hint: He'll work harder than ever. Happily.
choices.text: A little shop near the house. He works there seven days a week now, and he's never been happier.

choices.label: 'He likes working'
choices.text: 'He likes it,' {J} says. {MUM} goes quiet on the phone.

scenarios.title: Abuse From the Stands
text: In an away game, a section of the home crowd targets {J} with racist chants. The referee hears it. The match continues.

text.t: Racist abuse from the away end. Before {J} can react, {CAPl} walks over to the referee and the whole team follows. Nobody plays until something is done.

choices.label: Walk off the pitch
choices.text: He walks. Some teammates follow. The match is suspended. It's on every channel in the world, and most of them are on his side.

choices.label: Report it and keep playing
choices.text: He tells the referee, points at the stand, and plays on. Afterwards he posts a long, calm statement. The league opens an investigation.

choices.label: Answer with a goal
choices.text: He doesn't say a word. The next time he gets the ball, he plays like his life depends on it.

scenarios.title: An Old Teammate Asks for Help
text: A teammate from {FIRSTCLUB}'s youth team never made it. Now he's driving a taxi and asks, embarrassed, if {J} knows anyone who needs a driver.

text.t: An old youth-team friend has seen the foundation's work and asks if there's a job there. He's good with kids. He's had a hard few years.

choices.label: Give him a real job
choices.text: He starts on Monday. He's punctual, grateful and funny. Within a year he's indispensable.

choices.label: Make some calls for him
choices.text: Two calls, one recommendation. He gets a job at a club's academy. He sends a photo in his new tracksuit.

choices.label: Give him money and wish him luck
choices.text: He takes the money, thanks him, and doesn't call again. {J} isn't sure if he helped or hurt.

scenarios.title: Among the Best in the World
text: The debate has started: is {J} one of the best players in the world? Pundits argue about him on three continents.

text.t: An Indonesian among the world's best. The country can barely believe it. Every coffee stall has his face on the TV.

scenarios.prompt: The world is talking about you.

choices.label: Embrace it
choices.desc: 'I want to be the best. Why hide it?'
choices.text: His bold quote is everywhere. Now every game is a referendum on it.

choices.label: Deflect to the team
choices.desc: 'Talk to me when we win something.'
choices.text: The humility makes the debate louder. His teammates love him for it.

scenarios.title: A Giant Is Watching
text: The sporting director of one of the world's biggest clubs is in the stand. {J}'s agent texts before kick-off: 'Don't look up. Just play.'

text.t: Reports say the biggest clubs in Europe are compiling dossiers on {J}. His manager is asked about it in every press conference.

choices.label: Tell your agent: push for it
choices.hint: Your club may not like it.
choices.text: Your agent starts talking. Your club starts worrying. Offers will come from abroad — and from the very top.

choices.label: Commit to your club publicly
choices.text: 'I'm happy here.' The fans sing his name louder than ever. The giants will come back.
